in_sanskrit.name: पद्मप्रिया
in_sanskrit.long_meaning:
पद्म् (Padma) - lotus,
प्रिया (Priya) - dear, loving

So, Padmapriya means 'Loving Goddess Padma (Lotus)'.

in_hindi.name: पद्मप्रिया
in_hindi.long_meaning:
पद्म (Padma) - कमल (Lotus),
प्रिया (Priya) - प्यारी (Beloved, Dear, Loving)

So, Padmapriya in Hindi means 'Beloved Lotus'.

in_tamil.name: பத்மப்ரியா
in_tamil.long_meaning:
பத்மம் (Padamam) - கமலம் (Lotus),
பிரியா (Priya) - வளர்ந்து வரும் வந்திருக்கின்ற ஒன்பது (Beloved, Dear, Loving)

So, Padmapriya in Tamil means 'Beloved Lotus'.

in_telugu.name: పద్మప్రియా
in_telugu.long_meaning:
పద్మ (Padma) - కెయ్యెడు (Lotus),
ప్రియా (Priya) - ప్యారే (Beloved, Dear, Loving)

So, Padmapriya in Telugu means 'Beloved Lotus'.

in_marathi.name: Padmapriya
in_marathi.long_meaning: Padmapriya हे एक हिंदू नाव आहे जे भारतीय संस्कृतीत खोल आध्यात्मिक महत्त्व ठेवते। Padma (lotus) represents purity, knowledge, and enlightenment. Priya means love. Thus, Padmapriya signifies the love for knowledge, purity, and enlightenment.

data.cultural_impact: The name Padmapriya holds significant value in Hindu culture, where the Padma symbol is revered. Lotus flowers are commonly used in religious rituals, art, and architecture due to their pure white color, fragrance, and significant connection to various Hindu deities, particularly Lakshmi, Saraswati, and Vishnu. The name Padmapriya connects the person to this rich cultural heritage and ideals of knowledge, purity, and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Padmapriya has deep spiritual significance. The lotus symbolizes detachment, creation, purity, and rebirth. In Hinduism, the lotus is often associated with the divine, representing the spiritual potential that lies within all us. Padmapriya may be seen as a reminder to constant self-improvement, seek knowledge, maintain purity in thoughts and actions, and eventually achieve spiritual enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: Padmapriya was a celebrated dancer in the royal courts of the Chola dynasty in the late 10th and early 11th centuries. She was renowned for her exquisite dance performances, which were often depicted in temple carvings and inscriptions.

historical_references.reference: Padmapriya was a legendary figure in ancient Hindu texts, described as a beautiful and virtuous woman who was the consort of the god Vishnu in his avatar as Krishna. She is often depicted in Hindu mythology as the embodiment of love and devotion.
